angle: The summer hold-out: Isak stopped training with Newcastle, went public with 'promises were broken', Newcastle said no promise was ever made, and he still left on deadline day for a British record £125m. Fifteen months later he has 10 goals this season for Liverpool.
why_now: In the news this week: scored twice in Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool in the Champions League on 25 Nov 2026, taking him to 10 goals this season (BBC Sport 'All coming together - Isak repaying Liverpool faith', Guardian match report). Reddit digest failed today (RSS 404 / JSON 403) and there is no trends file for today, so this was picked from the BBC Sport football index. Last Scout File was Bayern (Kane); Liverpool last used on 18 Nov (Wirtz).
open_loop: He stopped training with Newcastle and said trust was lost. Newcastle said he wasn't for sale. Two weeks later he was the most expensive signing in British history. How did the stand-off end?
hook_suggestion: He stopped training with Newcastle. Then cost a British record £125m.

beats.fact: In summer 2025 Alexander Isak stood off with Newcastle, training away from the group and not playing for them this season, to force a move to Liverpool. On transfer deadline day, 1 September 2025, Liverpool signed him for a British record fee of £125m.

Voice (max 12 words): 'He skipped an awards night to say: promises were broken.' On 19 August 2025 Isak did not attend the PFA awards, where he was named in the Premier League team of the season, and posted a statement on Instagram saying promises had been broken and trust lost (long quote goes on the card).
beats.quote: When promises are broken and trust is lost, the relationship can't continue.

beats.fact: Newcastle hit back the same night: Isak was under contract and 'no commitment has ever been made by a club official' that he could leave that summer. They had already rejected Liverpool's £110m bid on 1 August and said they did not foresee the conditions for a sale being met.
beats.quote: We are clear in response that Alex remains under contract and that no commitment has ever been made by a club official that Alex can leave Newcastle United this summer.

beats.fact: Newcastle signed striker Nick Woltemade from Stuttgart and Yoane Wissa from Brentford, and Liverpool came back. On deadline day Isak had a medical, signed a six-year contract and became a Liverpool player for a British record £125m. Newcastle's announcement was a terse 37-word statement.
beats.quote: I want to create history. I want to win trophies.
beats.note: 37-word statement is BBC only: use on card only as 'Newcastle's statement: short' or drop if the writer needs strict 2-source; the fee, six-year contract and Woltemade/Wissa signings are in both.

beats.fact: Isak scored twice as Liverpool won 3-0 at Club Brugge in the Champions League on 25 November 2026, taking his tally for the season to 10 goals.
beats.quote: He is in a great moment right now.
